newsitem.title: USA: Photran Q1 hurt by lower prices, charge.
newsitem.headline: Photran Q1 hurt by lower prices, charge.

text.p: Photran Corp said Monday its loss for the first quarter reflects lower unit prices and production levels, as well as a $200,000 charge related to cancelled products and the termination of a building lease.
Earlier, Photran reported a net loss of $0.23 a share, compared with a year-ago net loss of $0.07. Quarterly net sales were $523,869, down from $677,459 a year ago.
Photran said previously it expected to record a loss for the first quarter.

Photran had restated its 1996 results after it discovered alleged accounting and financial irregularities. The comapny previously said the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission was formally investigating the irregularities.
The company reiterated that it expects to begin generating income in the latter half of 1997, thanks to productivity initiatives and the start-up of a second production line.

The company said it began test production on its new P-2 line and expects this second line to begin operating at full capacity in June. The line is to increase Photran's overall capacity by approximately 200 percent.
Over the past several weeks, Photran said, it has received initial orders from four new Asian customers. The orders total 70,00 units to be delivered in the second quarter.

As previously reported, Photran was served in May with a lawsuit against the company, its former chief executive officer, and certain Photran officers and directors. The suit alleges that Photran's registration statement and prospectus, as well as quarterly reports filed in 1996, contained false and misleading information.
Photran said it denies that the plaintiffs are entitled to any relief.
Photran develops, manufactures and markets high performance optical and electrically conducive thin film coated products.
